images.title: A double number line, kg above and g below
images.purpose: Show that every kilogram mark has a gram mark 1,000 times as big (4 kg and 4,000 g, 9 kg and 9,000 g, 16 kg and 16,000 g) and that going back is ÷ 1,000.
images.composition: Two long lines one above the other with four matching tick marks, the kg numbers on the top line, the g numbers on the bottom line, and two arrows.
images.exact_structure: Plain white frame, 1456 by 816. TOP LINE: a thin dark #1F2937 horizontal line at y 270 from x 130 to x 1326 with an open circle (14 px) at each end, and exactly 4 vertical tick marks (40 px tall, 4 px thick) at x 210, 557, 903, 1250, equally spaced (the marks are not drawn to scale). The unit word kg (40 px, bold, teal #0072B2) is at the left end, x 60, above the line. BOTTOM LINE: the same kind of line at y 500 with the same 4 tick marks at the same x positions, directly under the top ticks. The unit word g (40 px, bold, amber #E69F00) is at the left end, x 60, below the line. TOP LABELS (centred on the tick, 40 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 200): 1 kg at x 210; 4 kg at x 557; 9 kg at x 903; 16 kg at x 1250. BOTTOM LABELS (centred on the tick, 40 px, bold, dark #1F2937, about y 580): 1,000 g at x 210; 4,000 g at x 557; 9,000 g at x 903; 16,000 g at x 1250. ARROW: a dashed teal #0072B2 curved arrow from the top tick at x 557 down to the bottom tick at x 557, arrowhead at the bottom, with the label × 1,000 (40 px, bold, teal) beside its middle. ARROW: a dashed amber #E69F00 curved arrow from the bottom tick at x 903 up to the top tick at x 903, arrowhead at the top, with the label ÷ 1,000 (40 px, bold, amber) beside its middle. CAPTION at the bottom centre, y 740: the text kg to g: × 1,000; g to kg: ÷ 1,000 (40 px, bold, dark #1F2937). Nothing else in the frame.
labels: kg to g: × 1,000; g to kg: ÷ 1,000
rejection: any count of objects, cells, ticks or rows that differs from the numbers stated in the spec
any text beyond the listed visible text, or any listed text misspelled or altered
any board name, publisher name, book title, page number or curriculum branding anywhere in the frame
a hyphen used in place of a minus sign on any labelled number
any count of tick marks that differs from 4 on each line, or a tick on one line with no matching tick on the other
a kg number paired with a g number that is not 1,000 times as big
images.takeaway: Every kg number matches a g number 1,000 times as big, and going back from g to kg is dividing by 1,000.
images.description: A double number line with 1 kg, 4 kg, 9 kg and 16 kg above and 1,000 g, 4,000 g, 9,000 g and 16,000 g below, with a × 1,000 arrow and a ÷ 1,000 arrow.
images.context: Concept image for Kilograms and Grams. It follows the idea of the double number line in your maths book (kg above, g below, x1000) and uses the concept's own example (practice values).
images.teaching_notes: Point to a tick and read both numbers together. The slip to watch: thinking 1 kg is 100 g.

image_decisions.why: The matching ticks and the two arrows show the link between the two units as a picture.
